item.title: Memphis coach Penny Hardaway says he paid $2.6 million of his own money to Tigers' revenue share
item.description: Penny Hardaway is putting $2.6 million of his $2.9 million salary into Memphis Tigers revenue share as he fights to save his job in year nine.
item.content:encoded:
It is no secret that this upcoming college basketball season is a make-or-break year for Penny Hardaway and the Memphis Tigers, and the head coach is doing everything he can to make it a successful campaign, including putting nearly his entire annual salary back into the team's roster budget.

Hardaway, entering year nine as the Tigers' head coach, revealed to the Memphis Commercial Appeal during American Conference media day that he is contributing $2.6 million of his own money into Memphis' revenue share. His salary this season is $2.9 million, and the contribution brings the team's revenue share to $9 million, according to the outlet.

"They were saying if you want more money you have to put your money in. So I did," Hardaway told the Commercial Appeal, while also clarifying that the university did not ask him to make the contribution.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

Hardaway's contribution back into his program comes as the Tigers are welcoming nine newcomers via the transfer portal in 2026, with the group being headlined by forward Rihards Vavers from Washington State and point guard Brandin Cummings out of Pitt. Memphis is also hopeful Nemanja Popovic, who played professionally in Poland a season ago, takes the floor for the program this season.

The Tigers are coming off a 13-19 season, their worst record since Hardaway's arrival in 2018, and are not only looking to return to the NCAA Tournament this season, but also pick up a win during March Madness for just the second time under Hardaway.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

With Memphis being a city that eats and breathes the game of basketball and consistently produces top-tier talent, the Tigers should be a dominant force in what is now a well-below-average American Conference.

The Tigers seemed to be building something special in 2021 by winning the NIT and then advancing to the Round of 32 during the 2022 NCAA Tournament, but simply have not managed to take a step forward over the course of the last few seasons.

Hardaway is under contract until April 2028, and while the paper indicates that his job is secure beyond this season, he's well aware of what is at stake.

"I didn’t want to fail two years in a row, because I already know what that means for me," Hardaway shared with the Commercial Appeal.

With Hardaway being a Memphis native and a Tiger legend himself, it has felt like he's been given the benefit of the doubt when other coaches in his situation would not have been, but another season without an NCAA Tournament berth could be the end of his run in the 901.

item.title: GOP governor candidate skips debate against former Biden advisor, replaced by empty podium
item.description: Georgia Republican gubernatorial candidate Rick Jackson did not attend a debate, leaving Democratic rival Keisha Lance Bottoms next to an empty podium at the event.
item.content:encoded:
Georgia Republican gubernatorial candidate Rick Jackson did not appear for a scheduled debate Monday night, leaving his Democratic opponent, Keisha Lance Bottoms, answering questions next to an empty podium.

"Rick Jackson is the first gubernatorial candidate not to stand here in 32 years," Bottoms said during the forum, claiming that Jackson would "rather hide behind his billions than explain to you his record of making billions off the taxpayers of Georgia. While he is running to enrich himself, I am running to be your governor."

LGBTQ GROUP REVEALS WHICH DEM NOMINEE IS SPONSORING HALLOWEEN EVENT FEATURING DRAG SHOWS

The Atlanta Journal-Constitution reported that organizers indicated Jackson would become the first major-party gubernatorial candidate not to attend an Atlanta Press Club general election debate in the history of the outfit's debate series. Press Club officials said that there was an attempt to set up a gubernatorial debate in 1994, but neither the Democrat incumbent nor the GOP rival could participate, according to the association.

Jackson's campaign did not immediately respond to Fox News Digital's request for comment.

On Monday, Jackson said that he had "not had one voter ask me a question about debate. That's not what's important to them. What's important to them is affordability and gas prices going up."

DHS ISSUES SCATHING REBUKE AFTER FORMER ATLANTA MAYOR KEISHA LANCE BOTTOMS TOUTS CUTTING TIES WITH ICE

Bottoms has served as Atlanta mayor and as a senior advisor to President Joe Biden for public engagement. Jackson is a businessman and philanthropist.

The rival candidates previously participated in an Atlanta News First town hall-style debate event on Oct. 6 in which they fielded questions from voters.

TRUMP'S ENDORSEMENT FAILS TO SAVE MAGA CANDIDATE AS BILLIONAIRE ADVANCES IN KEY GOVERNOR RACE

President Donald Trump endorsed Jackson after the candidate defeated Georgia Lt. Gov. Burt Jones, who Trump backed for the Republican gubernatorial primary and primary runoff.

item.title: Sean McVay is 'sick' about his overtime call as another Super Bowl coach publicly regrets end of game decision
item.description: Sean McVay says he's "sick" after a third-down play call led to a blocked field goal in the Rams' overtime loss to the Buffalo Bills on Monday.
item.content:encoded:
Week 5 of this NFL season will be remembered by historians as the week when head coaches apologized, admitted mistakes and otherwise regretted their decisions in front of their teams and in public — and Los Angeles Rams coach Sean McVay is the latest to join them.

The Rams lost in overtime to the Buffalo Bills in what was perhaps the most entertaining game of the season on Monday Night Football.

Afterward, McVay was unhappy with himself, saying he was "sick" and "regretting" a decision that wasn’t necessarily wrong but wasn’t optimal and didn’t help his team in what could have been a game-deciding situation.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

Here's the situation:

The game is in overtime. The Rams have stopped the Bills on their first possession, so any points by McVay's team wins the game.

And the Rams seem headed toward those points and victory when they drive from their 20-yard line to the Buffalo 30 mostly by attempting five consecutive pass plays.

The Buffalo defense is on its heels under Matthew Stafford’s passing barrage. But on third-and-5 from the Bills' 30-yard line, McVay calls a run for Kyren Williams off right tackle.

No gain.

It was, clearly, the coach setting his team up for a field goal rather than pressing the issue. Except the Rams had their field goal blocked on fourth down, continuing a multi-season struggle with their special teams that has cost them multiple games.

"Yeah, you know what? If I would have known," McVay told reporters afterward. "I wish I would have had a better play call and gone for it, got it a lot tighter. I'm sick right now with myself.

"...I'm proud of the way that we battled and I'm sick that we came up short and I'll be regretting kicking that and not having a better call to be able to go forward on third down ...

"That's on me."

We heard this multiple times in Week 5.

Washington Commanders coach Dan Quinn said "it's my responsibility" for the blown clock management at the end of his team's game against the New York Giants that turned a likely victory into a tie.

Philadelphia Eagles coach Nick Sirianni took blame for his team's last-second loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars because of a decision he made on a kickoff.

"I lost us that game," Sirianni said.

NICK SIRIANNI MAKES DECISON THAT OPENED THE DOOR TO A JACKSONVILLE JAGUARS COMEBACK WIN

These coaches are seemingly wrestling each other for Harry Truman's "The Buck Stops Here" Oval Office sign. And that's good.

Accountability from a head coach, especially when it is taken publicly, sets a good example for players and how they'll act privately within the team.

But that's not the point.

The point is three coaches that took teams to the Super Bowl — McVay and Sirianni won on the NFL's grandest stage — made significant errors on the same week of NFL action. The mistakes were so obvious that all decided to take responsibility publicly.

The NFL last week was mired in officials making mistakes and getting suspended and that was the big story.

These star coaches all blowing it on the same week has shifted the focus to the quality of decisions by coaches in the league.

item.title: Actor Dan Levy blasts Shane Gillis' 'SNL' monologue, claims men's 'complacency' fuels sexual assault
item.description: Dan Levy accused Shane Gillis of misogyny over his "Saturday Night Live" monologue about women's gym attire, saying men's complacency enables sexual assault.
item.content:encoded:
"Schitt's Creek" star Dan Levy blasted comedian Shane Gillis on Sunday over his controversial "Saturday Night Live" monologue about women's gym attire, accusing him of misogyny and arguing that men's failure to challenge such remarks contributes to an environment in which women are sexually assaulted.

Levy, who hosted the NBC sketch comedy show in 2021, posted an Instagram video condemning Gillis' remarks on the latest episode and calling on other men to speak out against the comedian.

"I’m speechless that something like that can exist on live national television," Levy said. "And to be perfectly honest, more men need to be standing up in opposition to it because it’s complacency that has created the environment in which women are sexually assaulted, and it’s a ‘conversation’ as opposed to a ‘crime.’"

WATCH: SHANE GILLIS REJECTS UFC FIGHTER’S CRUDE MICHELLE OBAMA JAB AFTER WHITE HOUSE WIN

Gillis sparked controversy Saturday while hosting "SNL" for the third time. During his opening monologue, the comedian joked about going to public gyms in New York City before turning his attention to women's revealing workout clothing.

"I haven’t been to the gym in so long. I didn’t know women just dress like whores now?" Gillis said. "Look, I’m sorry, there’s no other way to describe [it]. Have you seen it? I’ve seen it. You’ve seen the shorts? They’re those neon, like, artificial bait-colored [shorts], and the wrinkles go around the cheeks and all combine at the butthole. And don’t look! You’re not allowed to look."

Levy rejected the suggestion that revealing workout clothing justified Gillis' characterization, arguing that the comedian's comments reflected a broader problem with how men perceive women.

"Women wearing short shorts at the gym does not make them whores. It makes the men calling them whores misogynists," Levy said. "There’s a difference there. By the way, I’ve seen more men’s nipples at the gym than I’ve ever seen women showing their bodies off."

SOPHIE CUNNINGHAM SAYS WHAT OTHER GASLIGHTING FEMALE ATHLETES WON'T ABOUT THE NAKED SYDNEY SWEENEY AD

Lisa Cusack, president of the Don't L.A. My Burbank PAC, pushed back against Levy's criticism in a statement to Fox News Digital, arguing that noticing revealing clothing does not automatically constitute misogyny.

"I don’t think it’s an either/or. A woman wearing a skimpy outfit isn’t necessarily a whore, and a man noticing that she’s using sex to get attention isn’t automatically a misogynist," Cusack said. "In our social media world, there’s a glut of sexualized images women feel they have to compete with, but if you dress like a sex object on a screen, men are going to respond in a two-dimensional way."

COMEDIAN TIM DILLON SLAMS SYDNEY SWEENEY CRITICS UPSET WITH STEAMY AD: 'HOW INSANE IS THAT?'

Levy argued that objectifying women in entertainment contributes to how they are treated outside the media, insisting that men have a responsibility to challenge such behavior.

"This is not a women’s issue; this is an everybody issue. Because the more that men objectify women in the media, the more that other men see them as objects and treat them as objects," Levy said. "They are not objects. They are superior human beings to men, OK? And I’m sorry if this gets me in trouble with the internet, but f---."

Cusack offered a different perspective on sexuality and social expectations, arguing that modern culture has increasingly abandoned restraint and mystery.

"Sometimes we forget that glamour is the opposite of pick-me energy. Glamour is controlling perception with a little bit of mystery," Cusack added. "In losing this, we lose a lot of romance, and everything gets stripped down — no pun intended — to its most vulgar form." 

Fox News Digital reached out to NBC for comment. Gillis' team declined to comment.

item.title: Stephen A Smith issues another serious apology, this one about a colleague's divorce
item.description: Stephen A. Smith admitted to sharing inaccurate divorce details about Iman Shumpert and Teyana Taylor on his "The Culture Table" podcast episode.
item.content:encoded:
Stephen A. Smith had to issue two apologies last week after insensitive comments about Lane Johnson's mental health, but he had another mistake to own up to earlier this week.

The ESPN mogul recently helped launch a new podcast, "The Culture Table," and in a recent episode, Smith discussed the divorce of former NBA player and current ESPN analyst Iman Shumpert and Teyana Taylor.

On his own self-named podcast, Smith admitted to sharing "inaccurate" information about their divorce.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

"In the interest of fairness, accuracy, and decency, I believe it’s important to address what happened in an October episode of 'The Culture Table' titled, ‘Can Men Trust Women With Their Finances?' During that episode, I stated that Teyana Taylor walked away from her divorce with $25 million, $10 million in properties, luxury cars, and other assets, while Iman Shumpert, her ex-husband, was left with approximately $2 million and nowhere to live. Those statements were inaccurate, and I want to sincerely apologize to both Iman Shumpert and Teyana Taylor.

"Straight Shooter Media and I as the CEO have a responsibility to ensure that information presented is properly sourced. We didn’t meet that standard here, plain and simple."

Smith admitted he believed false quotes that were attributed to Shumpert and said he apologized to both of them personally. The episode has been taken down at Smith's request, he said.

THREE NFL TEAMS ROASTED FOR CELEBRATING INDIGENOUS PEOPLES' DAY ON COLUMBUS DAY, WHICH NO TEAM EVEN MENTIONED

"I also regret that the segment may have left viewers with the impression that Iman had publicly disparaged the mother of his children," Smith added.

This apology comes just days after Smith appeared to poke fun at the aforementioned Johnson, now a former Philadelphia Eagles lineman, retiring midseason to focus on his mental health in the midst of the Birds' struggles.

"Now he calls it quits. Not before the season. Not in the offseason," Smith said in a recent episode of "First Take." " ... Four games into the 2026 season, a dude that has been in the league forever sits back and says, ‘I need to focus on my mental health.’ Am I making it up?"

Smith doubled down, mocking the timing of Lane's decision: "And this brother said, ‘Hey, my life matters. It’s time. I’m gonna call it quits. My mental health. My mental.' Lord!"

Smith hopped on his podcast that night to apologize to Johnson and "for the misunderstanding regarding [his] comments." A further apology came at the beginning of the next day's "First Take" episode. Smith had even made sure to note shortly after his crack on Johnson that he was not "mak[ing] light of mental health issues" but instead "making light of the Philadelphia Eagles’ trashy situation right now."

item.title: Selma Blair accused of kicking nurse hours after JFK plane arrest
item.description: Selma Blair allegedly kicked a nurse in the chest at a Queens hospital hours after her arrest for an incident aboard a Delta flight to JFK Airport.
item.content:encoded:
Selma Blair's alleged airline assault did not end with the police. She is also accused of kicking a nurse in the chest at a Queens hospital hours after she was arrested following an alleged in-flight incident aboard a Delta flight from Los Angeles to New York.

The criminal court affidavit, filed in Queens Criminal Court, says registered nurse Ashley DeLeo was assisting in transporting Blair for further medical treatment at Jamaica Hospital Medical Center at approximately 2 a.m. ET on Oct. 12 when Blair allegedly kicked her.

"The defendant kicked complainant DeLeo in her chest," the affidavit stated, adding that the alleged conduct caused "substantial pain to her chest."

SELMA BLAIR ARRESTED AFTER IN-FLIGHT INCIDENT

Blair, 54, was arraigned Monday on two counts of second-degree assault after Port Authority police responded to a call about a "physically abusive passenger" aboard Delta Flight 938, which had arrived at John F. Kennedy International Airport from Los Angeles, officials said.

The "Cruel Intentions" and "Hellboy" actress was taken into custody at JFK and transported to a hospital for evaluation. Two flight attendants reported injuries, and one was taken to a hospital, according to officials.

FRONTIER PASSENGERS TACKLE MAN WHO ALLEGEDLY CHOKED OFF-DUTY FLIGHT ATTENDANT, TRIED TO OPEN DOOR MID-FLIGHT

The court document also alleges Blair kicked a Port Authority police officer while being moved from JFK Terminal 4 into an ambulance at the airport’s B22 exit ramp.

Police Officer Maria Suarez was helping secure Blair on a stretcher at approximately 11:50 p.m. ET when Blair allegedly "removed her leg from the stretcher straps and kicked Officer Suarez repeatedly about the face, neck and chest," according to the affidavit.

CHAOS ERUPTS ON AMERICAN AIRLINES FLIGHT AS UNRULY PASSENGER ALLEGEDLY BITES FELLOW TRAVELER MIDAIR

The affidavit says Suarez suffered swelling to her jaw and "substantial pain to her face, neck and chest." Suarez was treated at a local Queens-area hospital, according to the filing.

Delta said in a statement Monday that it has "zero tolerance for unruly or unlawful behavior, as the safety of our customers and crew always comes first."

UNITED FLIGHT FROM CHICAGO MAKES EMERGENCY LANDING AFTER PASSENGER'S 'MULTIPLE ATTEMPTS' TO BREACH COCKPIT

A representative for Blair said the actress suffered a medical emergency during the flight.

"Selma experienced a medical emergency that led to the alleged conduct," Blair’s representative said. "Upon landing, she received immediate medical attention and is currently in stable condition."

SEVERE TURBULENCE DIVERTS NEW YORK CITY FLIGHT TO MIAMI, 8 INJURED

Blair’s attorney said in court that the incident was not intentional and argued that she had missed doses of a "powerful" medication used to control severe neurological symptoms.

"This was not an intentional assault," attorney Shawn Barnes said.

Barnes also said Blair had been working "extensive hours" before the flight and claimed she fell and hit her head during the trip.

"These factors, coupled with altitude, resulted in a state of severe confusion and disorientation," Barnes said.

SELMA BLAIR SAYS 'NO ONE RETURNED MY CALLS' AFTER ANTI-ISLAM COMMENT LED TO HOLLYWOOD FALLOUT

Blair has spoken publicly about her battle with multiple sclerosis, which she was diagnosed with in 2018. She was later released on bond and is expected back in court in January.

"I do believe she poses a risk," Judge Indira Kahn said Monday.

Reuters and The Associated Press contributed to this report.

item.title: Trump-linked super PAC pulls funding from 2 House Republicans as GOP fights to keep majority
item.description: House Republicans face growing pressure as Trump-aligned MAGA Inc. pulls planned spending from Tom Kean and Marianette Miller-Meeks' districts.
item.content:encoded:
A top elections group affiliated with President Donald Trump is halting spending planned in two key congressional districts held by sitting House Republicans as Election Day looms less than a month away.

MAGA Inc. is reallocating its planned investments in districts represented by Rep. Tom Kean, R-N.J., and Rep. Marianette Miller-Meeks, R-Iowa, for the remainder of the midterm election cycle, a source familiar with those plans confirmed to Fox News Digital.

A super PAC aligned with House GOP leadership, the Congressional Leadership Fund (CLF), is also pulling its cash from those districts to reroute into other races, a source familiar with those plans said.

Both groups will instead route those funds into other House races across the country. It comes after recent polling data signaled the two incumbents' chances for re-election have grown slim.

WATCH: BATTLEGROUND DEMOCRAT CALLED IOWA A 'BACKWATER' OVER TRANSGENDER ATHLETES BAN

Republicans' uphill battle to keep control of the House of Representatives is getting tougher by the day, according to various projections. The latest Fox News Power Rankings show Democrats having an edge in 219 House seats — enough to clinch a majority — while Republicans are projected to keep 198. Nineteen seats are still up in the air.

Kean's 7th Congressional District is one of the wealthiest in both New Jersey and the U.S. as a whole, encompassing suburbs and exurbs of New York City to the north.

A source close to Kean's campaign told Fox News Digital that "the race is fully funded down the home stretch."

Kean's campaign and House Republicans' campaign arm "have major reservations on broadcast," the source said, adding that his Democratic opponent Rebecca Bennett "has no soft dollar reservations on her behalf."

He and Miller-Meeks represent two of the most purple districts in the country.

Kean won his House seat in 2022 after defeating incumbent former Rep. Tom Malinowski, D-N.J., by less than 10,000 votes. His 2024 re-election margin was wider, winning by just over 5%, or 23,000 more votes than his Democrat challenger.

Miller-Meeks, meanwhile, is seeking a fourth term against Democrat Christina Bohannan, whom she defeated twice by roughly 20,000 and 800 votes in 2022 and 2024.

She first won in 2020 by just six votes — earning her the nickname "six-pack" among fellow House Republicans and GOP leadership.

DEMOCRATS SEE NEW CHANCES TO FLIP RED STATES — BUT A $400M GOP SPENDING ADVANTAGE COULD DERAIL THEIR PLANS

Miller-Meeks represents Iowa's 1st Congressional District in the state's southeast, encompassing the cities of Davenport and Iowa City.

The New York Times first reported plans by "top Republican super PACs aligned with President Trump and congressional Republican leadership" to pull funding from Kean and Miller-Meeks' districts over concerns about their polling.

TRUMP-LINKED MAGA INC POURS $10M INTO KEN PAXTON'S TEXAS SENATE RACE AGAINST JAMES TALARICO

CLF is reportedly pulling the funding as part of a wider reshuffling of its war chest into other districts that Republicans are more confident in.

That includes battleground Reps. Brian Fitzpatrick, R-Pa., and Monica De La Cruz, R-Texas, The Times reported.

item.title: 911 operators questioned whether Christa Pike failed execution call was prank, audio reveals
item.description: 911 audio reveals dispatchers initially dismissed Christa Pike's failed execution as a prank call, delaying the ambulance response to Riverbend Prison.
item.content:encoded:
911 dispatch recordings show a series of miscommunications led to delayed emergency response in the immediate aftermath of the Tennessee Department of Correction’s failed execution of death row inmate Christa Pike.

An initial 911 call came through to dispatchers around 8:40 p.m. on Sept. 30, roughly an hour after Pike’s planned execution began, according to documents and audio recordings obtained by Fox News. 

During the call, the unidentified caller informed operators of a failed execution but was unable to provide the operators with a code that would verify the legitimacy of the call.

Following that call, operators sought to determine the authenticity of the audio shows.

TENNESSEE DEATH ROW INMATE SURVIVES 2 LETHAL INJECTION DOSES IN FAILED EXECUTION ATTEMPT

"So we have a medical call for service at the Riverbend Prison," a dispatcher says in the Fox News-obtained audio.

The dispatcher explains to another operator that the caller said, "They carried out the execution, the subject didn’t pass away, and they need an ambulance because she’s not breathing normally."

DEATH ROW INMATE UNCONSCIOUS ON VENTILATOR AFTER BOTCHED EXECUTION FOR TEEN’S KILLING: ATTORNEYS

"We are trying to find out if that is an actual thing that is happening, and we need to send an ambulance, and/or if you need police assistance, or if this is someone that is just basically prank calling or like swatting us," the operator can be heard saying.

In another snippet of internal dispatcher audio, an operator can be heard calling off the emergency response.

TENNESSEE PRISON CHIEF RESIGNS AFTER FAILED EXECUTION AS FORMER US ATTORNEY TAPPED TO LEAD INDEPENDENT REVIEW

"Per supervisors here at the DEC [Department of Emergency Communications], we have been informed it is a false call," a dispatcher can be heard saying at approximately 9:03 p.m. "There is no medical assistance needed at Riverbend Prison."

An additional correspondence between an operator and what appeared to be somebody working at Riverbend Prison displayed further confusion.

CHRISTA PIKE'S FIRST WORDS REVEALED AFTER SHE UNEXPECTEDLY WOKE UP WHILE LAWYERS THOUGHT SHE WAS 'BRAIN DEAD'

"We got a call about a failed execution at your guys’ facility, and we’re just calling to verify," a dispatcher said.

"Um … who called you?" the prison employee responded.

"Is there like a sergeant I could speak with, or a supervisor?" the dispatcher asked.

"Who called you? Do you know?" the employee said.

"No, we don’t exactly know," the dispatcher replied.

"I’m being told nobody from our facility called you, so there’s not really anything to speak of at the moment," the employee said.

CHRISTA PIKE NOW CONSCIOUS AND TALKING AFTER SURVIVING 2 DOSES OF LETHAL INJECTION DRUG

Pike’s attorney Kelly Gleason also called 911 to report the botched execution, audio recordings prove.

"What’s going on is my client, Christa Gail Pike, is undergoing a state execution. She has completed the stages of the protocol and last we knew from the attorney who is present, she is still alive and breathing and needs immediate life-saving care," Gleason can be heard saying during a phone call timestamped at approximately 9:08 p.m.

CHRISTA PIKE'S ATTORNEY SAYS SHE'S 'UP AND WALKING' MORE THAN A WEEK AFTER BOTCHED EXECUTION

Around the same time as Gleason’s call, Riverbend Prison’s Central Control told emergency responders that they "would have been the ones to call in" but that they "did not make that call," according to the audio.

But also around that time, a first responder can be heard on a separate recording saying: "Somebody is outside the gate at the prison telling us that it’s real and demanding us to go in. They say they are some sort of state official. I need somebody to get out to the gate and talk to those people."

At that point, Central Control cleared the way for first responders to enter the prison at 9:11 p.m.

Pike was in an ambulance and being transferred to a hospital by 9:34 p.m., the Associated Press reported.

Pike was convicted of first degree murder and conspiracy to commit first degree murder in 1996 for the 1995 torture and murder of 19-year-old Colleen Slemmer. She was sentenced to death and had been on death row for over 30 years when she arrived at her scheduled execution by lethal injection on Sept. 30.

Prison execution authorities administered a single dose of pentobarbital, a central nervous system depressant used in Tennessee execution protocol. When Pike remained conscious after the initial dose, authorities administered a second dose per state protocol.

When the second dose did not kill Pike, Tennessee’s single-drug execution protocol prevented authorities from administering a third dose.

Pike was taken to a hospital where she was placed on a ventilator and remained unconscious for six days, waking up on Oct. 6, according to her attorneys.

Pike was taken back to the Debra K. Johnson Rehabilitation Center women’s prison on Oct. 10 where she is continuing to receive medical care, her attorneys said in a statement.

Following the failed execution, Tennessee Gov. Bill Lee has paused all state executions pending a further review.

Fox News Digital contacted the Tennessee Department of Correction and Pike’s attorneys for comment.

item.title: Man's fatal fall from Six Flags roller coaster sparks horrifying eyewitness accounts
item.description: Witnesses give accounts of a man falling to his death at Six Flags in Georgia. The company has temporarily closed similar roller coasters at multiple parks after the incident on the Goliath ride.
item.content:encoded:
Witnesses described horrifying scenes after a man reportedly fell to his death from a roller coaster at Six Flags Over Georgia — leaving other passengers stranded high above the ground.

The man was riding the roller coaster with his son, while his wife and daughter watched from the ground, according to an eyewitness account reported by local station WXIA.

The incident occurred around 4 p.m. Monday on the Goliath roller coaster at Six Flags Over Georgia.

TERRIFYING SCENE UNFOLDS AT SIX FLAGS AS STORM-TOPPLED TREE SENDS 4 GUESTS TO HOSPITAL

One witness told local outlet WXIA the man appeared in a souvenir photo taken during the ride.

"He was in our pictures," the witness said. "He fell and hit the car three different times."

Fox News Digital reached out to Six Flags for the latest on the ride's status.

Another couple who were on the ride described the terrifying moments surrounding the man's death, according to WXIA.

"The vehicle [meaning the ride] hit him, and then he flew back up again, and it hit him again, and then that's when he was, I guess, flung from the ride," the man told the outlet.

"It went from having a great time to just screaming, 'Oh my God, what is happening,'" his wife said. "You don't see things like this happen. It should never happen."

FRIGHTENING SCENE UNFOLDS ON ICONIC SKY RIDE AS CHILD FALLS DOWN ONTO BOARDWALK

Meanwhile, another Goliath rider said his train was ascending when passengers heard screaming and saw people running below. The ride then stopped, leaving them stranded for about an hour without updates.

"We were up there for an hour with no updates, no news, no nothing. We just saw everyone running out of the park," the witness told WXIA.

The Cobb County Police Department previously confirmed to Fox News Digital that one person died, and several others were reportedly injured. 

Police did not immediately provide further details about the circumstances surrounding the incident.

"We are deeply saddened by the guest incident at our park today," a Six Flags spokesperson previously told Fox News Digital.

WOMAN ALLEGEDLY EJECTED FROM ROLLER COASTER, SUFFERS SERIOUS INJURIES AFTER DRAGGED ALONG TRACK: REPORTS

"Our thoughts and heartfelt condolences are with the guest's family, friends and loved ones. We are also providing support to the guests and team members affected."

"Out of an abundance of caution, we have temporarily closed similar attractions across our parks," a Six Flags spokesperson said, according to the outlet.

"The safety of our guests and team members remains one of our highest priorities."

As of Tuesday morning, it was unclear which rides were temporarily closed. Six Flags Magic Mountain in California and Six Flags Great America in Illinois also have roller coasters named Goliath, though the attractions feature different designs.

The incident comes as Six Flags has been facing scrutiny over another roller coaster at its Magic Mountain park in California.

Six Flags Magic Mountain permanently closed its X2 roller coaster after multiple lawsuits accused the attraction of causing catastrophic brain injuries.

A spokesperson for Six Flags Magic Mountain confirmed earlier to Fox News Digital that X2 had not operated since July 12.

Dordick Law Corporation of Beverly Hills, which represents the plaintiffs, said it has retained more than 100 additional clients who allege they suffered brain injuries after riding X2, the firm told Fox News Digital on Sept. 23.

So far, three lawsuits have been filed.

Magic Mountain Park President Brian Oerding said the coaster consistently passed safety tests, but the park decided to close it amid concerns about guest confidence.

A Six Flags spokesperson previously declined to comment on pending litigation.

item.title: FBI operation targets scam compounds in Africa with arrests, account takedowns
item.description: Operation Blackout's latest raids across Ghana and Nigeria netted 28 arrests, freed trafficked workers and saw Meta remove 3.7 million accounts.
item.content:encoded:
The FBI's expanded global efforts to disrupt and dismantle sprawling scam compounds that prey on Americans netted multiple arrests in Africa last week, as well as millions of dollars in potentially freezable funds and the takedown of social media accounts tied to fraud, officials said.

Operation Blackout is the FBI’s global campaign to identify and dismantle foreign scam compounds through overseas raids, asset seizures and the disruption of web domains and infrastructure linked to scam networks.

Authorities also worked to rescue trafficked workers and return stolen money to victims.

"Thanks to a brilliant partnership with the Department of Justice, across multiple African countries, we arrested 28 alleged criminal actors, seized over 350 devices, identified at least $11 million in potentially freezable funds, freed over 100 trafficked workers, and identified over 100 potential scam victims here at home," FBI Director Kash Patel exclusively told Fox News Digital.

FIRST ON FOX: FBI TARGETS GHANA SCAM COMPOUND LINKED TO NEARLY $10M IN LOSSES, MORE THAN 130 DETAINED

"This is what happens when law enforcement executes with precision across the inter-agency," Patel added. "We are demolishing criminal scam centers across the globe and truly saving lives."

In a series of initiatives stemming from the larger FBI operation, authorities conducted law enforcement raids and seizures last week as part of a "Joint Disruption Week" based out of London that resulted in 28 arrests across Ghana and Nigeria.

GLOBAL PARTNERS ARE JOINING THE TRUMP ADMINISTRATION AND THIS FBI TO TAKE DOWN SCAM EMPIRES FOR GOOD

In addition to the arrests, authorities identified more than 100 scam victims with losses so far exceeding $10 million.

The more than 120 trafficked workers identified are slated to be repatriated, the FBI said.

Additionally, more than 3.7 million Facebook and Instagram accounts allegedly linked to fraudulent activity were taken down in partnership with Meta.

FBI WRAPS UP CYBERCRIME OPERATION TARGETING GLOBAL NETWORKS PREYING ON AMERICANS

"Scams are a global threat that demand a global response," Chris Sonderby, vice president and deputy general counsel for Meta, said in a news release from the tech giant regarding last week's operations. "Working with the U.K. National Crime Agency, the FBI, DOJ and the Homeland Security Task Force, we took the fight to scam centers across West Africa.

"As part of the disruption, we removed more than 3.7 million accounts, Pages and Groups targeting people in the U.S., U.K., and beyond, and shared leads on over 30 suspected scam centers resulting in dozens of arrests, the rescue of trafficking victims and cryptocurrency seizures," Sonderby added.

GLOBAL TASK FORCE DISMANTLES 'PIG-BUTCHERING' CRYPTO FRAUD RINGS PREYING ON AMERICANS

In Ghana, 117 victims are pending repatriation to Nigeria, and 19 suspects were arrested and detained. In Nigeria, local authorities will prosecute nine individuals arrested for violations of Nigerian law, the FBI said.

The Ghana and Nigeria operations follow a warning from Patel that international scam networks were expanding beyond Southeast Asia and the Middle East into Africa.

"That’s why you’re seeing the migration of these scam compounds to central and sub-Saharan Africa, which is where we are already pre-positioned to take them off," Patel told Fox News Digital in September.

The FBI-led initiative targets transnational cybercrime groups operating massive scam centers where trafficked workers are forced to carry out fraud schemes from thousands of miles away against unsuspecting Americans.

AMERICANS LOST OVER $20 BILLION TO ONE TYPE OF CRIME. HERE’S HOW WE CAN FIGHT IT

In total, Operation Blackout has resulted in roughly $17 billion being seized, hundreds of alleged scammers arrested and thousands of trafficked workers freed.

Furthermore, more than 10,000 Americans were warned about being targeted for potential fraud before losing their money, preventing an estimated $670 million in financial losses, according to the FBI.

Many of the victims are senior citizens, Patel previously told Fox News Digital. Criminal networks have begun a geographic shift in an effort to broaden their scams, Patel has said.

BURMA APPROVES DEATH PENALTY FOR SCAMMERS MONTHS AFTER FBI'S $8 BILLION CRYPTO CRACKDOWN

In September, a Justice Department Scam Center Strike Force team helped authorities in Madagascar take down 13 scam centers operated by Chinese organized crime syndicates and process more than 3,200 electronic devices, Fox News Digital previously reported.

Criminal networks have now begun using artificial intelligence to further their scams, experts said.

The technology gives scammers the ability to use voice cloning and send flawless emails and messages to potential victims, eliminating the language barriers that once made scams easy to spot.

"AI gives scam fighters powerful new tools," said Jack Stubbs, the lead scams investigator at OpenAI. "At OpenAI, we’re using AI to disrupt scam operations and help people spot scams. By sharing insights responsibly with industry and law enforcement partners, we can identify scam networks across platforms and build stronger collective defenses."

Fox News Digital's Brittany Miller and Ashley J. DiMella contributed to this report.

item.title: Trump asks Kimberly Guilfoyle to resign as Greece ambassador, White House confirms
item.description: Kimberly Guilfoyle faces allegations of a $100,000 payment request, diplomatic misconduct and hostile workplace claims at the U.S. Embassy in Greece.
item.content:encoded:
The White House has asked Kimberly Guilfoyle to resign as U.S. ambassador to Greece amid mounting allegations involving her financial dealings, treatment of embassy staff and relationships with foreign business interests.

"We have asked Ambassador Guilfoyle to resign. She has been a wonderful asset to the team, and we wish her well," White House press secretary Katie Zacharia announced Tuesday during her first-ever briefing to the press.

It is not clear whether Guilfoyle lodged her official resignation, and when asked for clarity, the White House referred Fox News Digital to the remarks from the briefing.

The update from Zacharia came just one day after President Donald Trump publicly acknowledged that he was considering firing Guilfoyle, who was previously engaged to his eldest son, Donald Trump Jr.

Trump further distanced himself from the ambassador when asked about the reports and her status with the first family. 

"Kimberly Guilfoyle — she was almost a member of your family. How surprised were you to learn about these allegations? What did you think?," a reporter asked Tuesday before he left for Alaska. 

"She wasn't a member of my family. She, I guess, dated my son a long time ago," Trump said. "She was doing a good job, but we didn't like what we were reading."

TRUMP 'LOOKING AT' FIRING AMBASSADOR TO GREECE: 'WE'RE NOT HAPPY'

Guilfoyle was with Donald Trump Jr. for six years, four of which they were engaged. They publicly split in December 2024, the same month Trump nominated her to serve as ambassador to Greece.

The ambassador came under scrutiny last week after The Wall Street Journal reported that she asked Trump donor Eric Deters to pay off a $100,000 American Express bill shortly before her Senate confirmation hearing in July 2025.

According to messages reviewed by the Journal, Guilfoyle urged Deters to wire the money directly to American Express, saying the transaction would not leave a paper trail, while offering to help him gain access to senior Trump administration officials. Deters said he never made the payment.

Guilfoyle's attorney, Jesse Binnall, disputed the authenticity of the messages, saying Guilfoyle had been paid to speak at events before her nomination and "was owed a balance for traveling to and supporting these patriotic events."

The allegations followed an earlier Journal investigation into Guilfoyle's conduct in Greece, including claims that she promoted the interests of Greek construction and energy company Aktor Group and allowed its registered lobbyist, Christos Marafatsos, to accompany her to private diplomatic meetings with senior officials.

The Journal also reported that Guilfoyle suggested at a dinner with Greek officials that the U.S. would undermine their government, citing political developments in Romania. Greece's foreign minister subsequently said there was no need to summon Guilfoyle for an explanation because the country's energy minister denied that any threat had been made.

Separately, the State Department's Office of Inspector General reportedly opened an investigation into allegations involving Guilfoyle's treatment of embassy employees, private travel, acceptance of gifts and relationships with business interests, according to the Daily Mail.

HOUSE DEMOCRAT INVESTIGATED OVER ALLEGED 'INAPPROPRIATE SEXUAL CONTACT' WITH STAFFER

Sources described a hostile workplace in which Guilfoyle allegedly threatened to fire employees. They also claimed that she demoted members of her security detail over minor incidents, including an officer who reportedly failed to answer a 4 a.m. request for ice while she was vacationing in Mykonos.

The inspector general's office declined to confirm or deny the existence of an investigation. Binnall told the Daily Mail that "any implication of wrongdoing by the Ambassador is unsupported."

The allegations drew scrutiny from congressional Democrats, including Sen. Jeanne Shaheen, D-N.H., and Rep. Gregory Meeks, D-N.Y., who called for a review of Guilfoyle's conduct. Meeks urged her removal if the allegations were substantiated.

Vice President JD Vance addressed the controversy Friday, cautioning against rushing to judgment while acknowledging that misconduct should carry consequences.

"Let's actually see what the facts are. Let's see what the truth is," Vance told reporters in Ohio. "And obviously, if there was something bad that happened, then people have to suffer consequences for it."

Secretary of State Marco Rubio, who visited Greece last week and delivered remarks against the backdrop of the Acropolis, initially defended Guilfoyle's performance.

"Our ambassador has been a strong ambassador here," Rubio told reporters Wednesday.

A day later, Rubio declined to address the allegations directly, challenging reporters over their reliance on unnamed sources. "You guys walk around thinking that because some source told you something, and you reported it, it's the gospel. It's not the gospel," Rubio said last Thursday. Just days later, the White House announced their request for her resignation.

Trump nominated Guilfoyle to the diplomatic post in December 2024. A former California prosecutor and longtime Trump ally, she previously served as a prominent surrogate and fundraiser for the president.

Before her engagement to Don Jr., Guilfoyle was previously married to California Gov. Gavin Newsom, a Democrat, from 2001 to 2006, when he served as mayor of San Francisco.

item.title: Massive bison rams pickup truck in Yellowstone after driver tries to avoid collision
item.description: A bull bison charged a man's Ford Ranger near Mud Volcano in Yellowstone National Park around 2:45 a.m. on Thursday — and fortunately, the man did not report injuries.
item.content:encoded:
A driver's early-morning trip through Yellowstone National Park took a frightening turn when a bison suddenly charged his pickup truck.

A video shared on Facebook shows the massive animal standing on a dark roadway before rushing toward the vehicle — then slamming into the front of the truck.

The driver had stopped his Ford Ranger after spotting the bull bison near Mud Volcano at around 2:45 a.m. on Thursday, according to Wyoming publication Cowboy State Daily.

YELLOWSTONE OFFICIALS DECIDE FATE OF BISON THAT LAUNCHED GRANDFATHER 8 FEET IN AIR

Kyle Weber, a seasonal mechanic who had been working in Yellowstone, was driving south from Canyon Village toward Fishing Bridge when he encountered the animal in the road, the outlet reported.

Rather than attempting to pass, he hit the brakes and waited for the bison to move.

"I slammed on my brakes and stopped, and was just sitting there watching and waiting for him to continue walking," Weber told Cowboy State Daily.

After he waited, the animal remained on the roadway — and then unexpectedly charged the pickup and hit its front-left side, according to the outlet.

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR LIFESTYLE NEWSLETTER

"I definitely got jolted," Weber said. "I knew they hit hard, but that was pretty rough."

Fox News Digital reached out to Yellowstone National Park for comment. 

Weber said he estimated the impact pushed his truck backward at least a foot and a half. The collision dented the truck's bumper and hood, and it broke a side marker light, according to Cowboy State Daily.

Weber reportedly plans to replace the damaged bumper and side marker, using the repairs as an opportunity to make some upgrades to the truck.

The dented hood, however, may remain as a reminder of the encounter.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE LIFESTYLE STORIES

"I think I'll keep it," Weber said. "It has a cool story behind it," the same outlet reported. 

"Not everyone can say they have bison damage decorating their vehicle," the publication noted.

Carl Isom-McDaniel was visiting the park with his grandson in July when a bull bison charged him at Bridge Bay Campground near Yellowstone Lake.

"They move faster than you could ever imagine," Isom-McDaniel later said from his hospital room. "As soon as he got off that tree, he launched me in the air."

Isom-McDaniel broke his femur in four places after being thrown into the air. He underwent surgery at a Montana hospital.

A photographer who witnessed the attack told Fox News Digital that Isom-McDaniel appeared focused on protecting his grandson. He asked about the boy immediately after the attack.

item.title: A little boy asked why his dad doesn't like him. His words broke my heart
item.description: Let me tell you about the hard work that we must do every day. Far too many of us make the mistake of trying to save young men only after they are broken.
item.content:encoded:
One of our young men came back from a day with the boys and told me he had to step away, so the child would not see him cry. The child, an 11-year-old with a buzzed head and a gap-tooth smile, told the young man that he loves coming around us because we feel like his uncles. Then the child got quiet. He said he gets sad sometimes because his dad never wants to talk to him or see him. What made the young man tear up was that the child then said that he hopes his father is doing good. "But why doesn’t my dad like me?"

We all love this young boy and there is nothing not to like about him. He is good to his mother. He tries hard at school. He stands up to bullies and takes care of those around him. This boy is only 11. He is asking for guidance. He is asking for adults to guide him. If we don’t step up, the streets will take him.

This is the hard work that we do every day. Far too many of us make the mistake of trying to save young men after they are broken. We hold the press conference after the shooting, myself included, and we say we must do better. We demand funding for programs after the arrest and the boy is long gone into the slammer. In the saddest cases, we write the obituary after the funeral and the family grieves over the senselessness. These tragedies happen because we often fail to build the boy before the streets define manhood for him.

CHICAGO PASTOR GATHERS HUNDREDS OF MEN TO DECLARE VIOLENCE-FREE ZONE ON SOUTH SIDE

By manhood I don’t mean puffing your chest like you're some bad dude. That’s an empty front. Manhood means discipline, responsibility, accountability, faith and all the qualities that allow one to stand strong on two feet. 

Every young boy learns from the men who stay and show how it is done. A young boy does not learn from a slogan, a speech or empty promises. The government can send a check, and it has sent more than its share into our neighborhood, but the government can never manufacture expectations. It cannot sit on the curb and talk to an 11-year-old boy who wants to know why his father disappeared.

Last week, I stood in front of our new Leadership and Economic Opportunity Center that we built to steward young boys like our 11-year-old. High up on one of the window panes, someone shot a hole through the glass. This is the third window pane that has been broken. We’re talking thousands to repair the damage and we will replace them.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE FOX NEWS OPINION

But think about what they shot. It wasn’t a liquor store or a vacant lot. It was a building — one of the first constructions on the South Side in who knows how long — going up where a motel notorious for crime once stood. And on a block that was known as America’s most dangerous. 

This building houses job training facilities, classrooms, tutoring, violence prevention and so on. Most of all, this building was built to house young boys and girls who need the safety to grow into strong, resilient adults. Someone looked at all of that and fired a bullet at it.

I’m ticked off and I'm upset. But I’m not quitting.

When that young man told me about that child and his father, I took that as a sign from God. I don’t know how, but I do know why and that is why I keep stepping forward. It is for these young boys. 

They need to see this building accomplished so they can understand what is expected of them in their lives. I know we cannot replace his father, but I know that we have no choice but to be vigilant with him and ensure that he grows up to be the father to his own son that he never had. That is our mission and we will not fail.

item.title: Sylvester Stallone calls himself an 'idiot' for doing his own stunts, details nine back surgeries

Sylvester Stallone admitted that he was an "idiot" for performing his own stunts after extensive medical procedures.

During an interview with Fox News Digital, the "Tulsa King" star opened up about the "millions" of regrets he has after decades of being an action star.

"Millions, millions of regrets. I could literally spend a half hour talking about injuries, the amount, not even like one, I'm talking about 30 hours, 30 minutes of just individual ones, because it becomes compounded. I have been injured many, many times, but after 'Expendables,' I ended up with nine back operations, three neck fusions. Both shoulders ripped out, eye, you know, all kinds of lens put ... it's been brutal," Stallone began.

Stallone admitted that he's never been "quite the same" since the surgeries.

SYLVESTER STALLONE REVEALS SURPRISING HEALTH STRUGGLE BEHIND HIS FAMOUSLY RIPPED PHYSIQUE

"Now you have to like make peace with the pain as much as you can," he shared.

WATCH: Sylvester Stallone calls himself an 'idiot' for doing his own stunts

The biggest lesson he has now, at 80 after decades of crazy stunt work, is to "let other people do their job."

"Don't be a stage hawk, or whatever you call it, a showboat. I know a lot of people are thinking about doing stunts ... don't. Don't. Let the pro do it," Stallone said. "Let me explain something, you cannot beat gravity, when you hit the ground, you lose, and it's going to come back."

He continued, "I mean, just ask every football player in the world. So yeah, that and people go, 'Aren't you proud of them?' No. I think I'm an idiot for doing that. I'm proud that I broke myself in pieces. Like, duh, no."

The Stallone-led "Tulsa King" is gearing up to release its fourth season on Oct. 16. The actor told Fox News Digital what still excites him about his character, Dwight Manfredi.

"He still hasn't achieved his goal, just when he thinks he's arrived, another situation, another dramatic episode presents itself, which is exactly what the show needs. We don't want him to be like, 'I can finally exhale.' No, you don't wanna," Stallone said.

item.title: Stop losing photo quality when you share pictures
item.description: iOS 27 finally lets iPhone Shared Albums store photos and videos at full resolution in iCloud, but new items count toward the owner's storage.
item.content:encoded:
You take a great photo, send it to someone and then hear the question nobody wants to hear: "Why does this look blurry?" That can happen because some sharing methods resize or compress photos before they reach the other person. The image may still look fine on a phone screen, but zoom in or try to print it and the lost detail becomes easier to spot.

With iOS 27, Apple is addressing one long-standing version of that problem. Shared Albums can now store newly added photos and videos in their original formats at full resolution. Samsung Galaxy and Google Pixel phones also have built-in ways to send photo files without relying on a messaging app that may shrink them along the way.

HOW TO SEARCH ANYTHING ON IPHONE, GALAXY AND PIXEL

Before iOS 27, Apple’s Shared Albums reduced photo resolution. Photos were generally limited to 2,048 pixels on the long edge, while videos could be delivered at resolutions up to 720p. Starting with iOS 27, newly shared photos and videos in the upgraded Shared Albums experience are stored in iCloud in their original formats at full resolution. That means newly shared photos can remain at their original resolution instead of being reduced to the limits used by older Shared Albums.

There is one trade-off. New items added to an upgraded Shared Album count toward the album owner’s available iCloud storage, including items other participants add. Items that were already in the album before the upgrade do not count toward that storage, and temporary Shared Albums do not count either.

First, make sure Shared Albums are enabled on your iPhone.

On an iPhone running iOS 27:

Apple requires iCloud Photos for the new Shared Albums experience in iOS 27.

Any new Shared Album you create in iOS 27 automatically uses Apple’s upgraded Shared Albums experience.

To create one:

Photos and videos you add to that new album are stored in their original formats at full resolution. You can also allow people to join through a link. Apple says friends and family can access and contribute to a shared album on the web even if they do not have an Apple Account or Apple device.

YOUR PHONE CAN FIX BADLY FRAMED PHOTOS AFTER YOU TAKE THEM

Albums created before iOS 27 stay in the older format until you upgrade them. Apple lets the owner upgrade an existing Shared Album to the new experience. After the upgrade, newly added photos and videos can be stored at full resolution. That word "newly" is important. Upgrading an album does not restore the original resolution of photos or videos that were already uploaded under the older system. So, if you have an older family album or vacation album and want future additions preserved at full quality, upgrading it makes sense.

If someone shares a photo through an upgraded Shared Album, you can save it to your own library.

Apple says photos and videos in the new Shared Albums experience can be stored at full resolution in their original formats. However, content saved from a Shared Album may not include every piece of information contained in the original file. That means Shared Albums are much better for preserving image quality in iOS 27, but I would still keep the original file if you want the most complete archival copy.

Shared Albums solve one specific problem, but they do not guarantee that every photo you send from an iPhone stays untouched. The method you choose still affects what the recipient gets. Messaging services can resize or recompress images depending on the service, connection and receiving device. We have previously covered how to send high-quality photos from an iPhone, including ways to get better results when sharing between iPhone and Android. If image quality is important, sending the actual file through a file-sharing tool is usually a safer choice than assuming a messaging app will preserve every pixel.

Samsung Galaxy phones include Quick Share, which sends photos, videos and other files directly to nearby devices. Quick Share can send the original file without putting it through the kind of image compression you may encounter in some messaging apps. That makes it a good option when you want to preserve the quality of a photo.

To send a photo with Quick Share:

Depending on the receiving device, Galaxy users can also create a QR code through Quick Share, so the other person can connect and receive the file.

Pixel phones also use Quick Share for nearby file transfers.

To send a photo:

Quick Share can send photos, videos and other files directly to nearby Android devices, Chromebooks and supported Windows computers. You can also create a QR code if the receiving device does not appear right away. The other person scans the code to connect and receive the files.

Quick Share has become more useful if your household mixes Android and Apple devices. Google says Pixel 8a and later and certain supported Android phones can use Quick Share with compatible Apple devices through AirDrop. The iPhone, iPad or Mac user needs to set AirDrop to Everyone for 10 Minutes before the Android user sends the file.

On Android:

Devices that do not support the direct connection can still use Quick Share’s QR-code option. Google says those files are end-to-end encrypted and remain available for download for 24 hours. That can save you from emailing photos to yourself or putting them through a social app when you want to move the original file between platforms.

There is a reason photo-sharing services have compressed images for years. Full-resolution files take up more space. A smartphone photo can be several megabytes, while RAW images are much larger. High-resolution video can use hundreds of megabytes or more. In iOS 27, new photos and videos added to an upgraded Shared Album count toward the album owner’s iCloud storage. That includes new items other participants contribute. If you start creating large Shared Albums, check Settings > your name > iCloud from time to time so you know how much storage you have left.

Probably not. If you are sending a quick snapshot to a friend, and they will only look at it on their phone, some compression may never be noticeable. Full quality becomes more useful when you plan to print a photo, crop into a small detail or keep an important image for years. The same thinking applies to video. A smaller copy may work fine for a quick message, while the original file makes more sense if you plan to edit it later or watch it on a larger screen. Choosing the right sharing method depends on what you plan to do with the file after it arrives.

I like this iOS 27 change because Shared Albums have always been convenient, but their old resolution limits could make them a poor place to keep the best version of an important photo. Full-resolution sharing removes that problem for newly added photos and videos. Galaxy and Pixel users already have a strong option with Quick Share when the goal is sending the actual file without routing it through a messaging app. When photo quality counts, pay attention to how you send the file. There is a storage cost to keeping everything at full resolution, especially with video. Still, for wedding photos or family memories you may want to print later, I would rather preserve the original detail and decide what to compress afterward.

item.title: Judge Judy fires back at critics over America remarks: ‘It’s gonna take a lot more’ to shut me up
item.description: Judge Judy fired back at Sunny Hostin and Ana Navarro after "The View" hosts sharply criticized her love-it-or-leave-it remarks about America.
item.content:encoded:
EXCLUSIVE — Judge Judy Sheindlin responded to the furor caused by her love-it-or-leave-it remarks about America last month, explaining that she wasn’t calling America "perfect," but that the country is based on certain principles she is compelled to defend.

"I have a house, and I have a home. I consider America my home," Sheindlin told USA Today in the now-viral interview exchange. "America has been good to me. I think that it’s the greatest country in the world."

"If you don’t like this country, go somewhere else," she continued. "Don’t come to the greatest country in the world, the most successful country in the world, and say, ‘I want to change it.’ There are other countries that are the something else that you want. Go there. Go there. But don’t come into my home and say, ‘I want to change it.’"

JUDGE JUDY SAYS THOSE WHO DON'T LIKE AMERICA SHOULD 'GO SOMEWHERE ELSE'

ABC's "The View" dedicated a whole segment to Sheindlin’s take. While Sara Haines and Alyssa Farah Griffin came to her defense, Sunny Hostin and Ana Navarro expressed disappointment with the judge’s words. Hostin even said she detected "selfishness" in her comments, arguing that they focused too much on individual success. She suggested that patriotism means fighting to make your country better for everyone.

"I take umbrage with what she said, and I don’t like it at all," Navarro also said of Judge Judy’s remark, adding that it’s because she loves America that she feels she has "the duty and responsibility to call out the grift and the cruelty and the racism and the abuses of power and the anti-American actions that [Trump] is taking on."

Sheindlin said she didn’t understand Hostin’s response.

"If you listen to what I said, I was saying my country is America," she told Fox Digital. "Every American should feel that way. And America is my home. Everybody should feel that way. So, when I said ‘my,’ I wasn’t limiting it to myself."

'THE VIEW' CO-HOST ANA NAVARRO OFFERS ONE KEY REASON FOR WHY SHE STILL IDENTIFIES AS A REPUBLICAN

Of Navarro, Sheindlin said she takes everything she says with "a grain of salt."

"I accept criticism, and you can criticize my view, which was not that the country is perfect — and I did say in that interview that there’s nothing wrong with tweaking this country," Sheindlin told Fox News Digital of the backlash in general. "Everything can always be better. I mean, if you live in a house — which I compared America to — if you live in a house, the house could always be better. It could use a fresh coat of paint every once in a while. Sometimes it needs new carpeting. Sometimes it will need a new stove or refrigerator to keep it functioning optimally. You have to upgrade your television sets or else you won’t be able to get certain programming and high definition. That’s tweaking."

But, she added, "There’s a difference between tweaking your house and burning it down."

"And this country was founded on certain principles," she continued. "And where those principles are being tested and saying those are not the right principles. I mean, if you’re a capitalistic country, you’re not a socialistic country."

MORE AMERICANS THAN EVER NOW HAVE A POSITIVE VIEW OF SOCIALISM, NEW POLL SAYS

"The basis of this country is a capitalist country," she continued. "And when you say, ‘Well, we don’t want capitalism anymore, we want socialism,’ that’s where I draw the line. Because then you are fiddling around with what this country is about."

Socialism, she said, is not popular with the vast majority of Americans, musing that most people agreed with her statement. 

"The very vocal minority won’t address the statement," she said. "They try to shut you up by giving you a negative name, by calling you names which they hope will lead you to shut up. Not responding to the message and saying, ‘Judy, I understand what you’re saying, but not everyone comes from a background where they see their life being fulfilled in this country… so that everyone has potential to reach the American Dream.’"

That’s an argument that Sheindlin said she understands.

"But to call me a name because I said this is a great country and tweak it, but don’t burn the house down?" she asked.

"It’s gonna take a lot more than Ana Navarro to shut me up," she added.

Fox News Digital has reached out to "The View" for comment.

JUDGE ADAM LEVY PREVIEWS HIS ‘NITTY-GRITTY’ NEW SHOW – AND HOW HIS STYLE COMPARES TO HIS MOM JUDGE JUDY

"It’s one of the sad things about this internet, which has the capacity to do so many good things and join people together," Sheindlin said. "It has allowed some people, either anonymously or overtly, to be mean-spirited."

Sheindlin’s special, "Judge Judy: Unfiltered, Unforgettable," aired on CBS in late September.

"I think that the people who are fans over the years sort of got to know that what you see is what you get," she said. "The naysayers probably would not watch. If you’re not somebody’s cup of tea … I can skip it. I think that fans who watched the special and have been following me over the last 25 years or 30 years or newcomers for less time, I believe that they know who I am."

"My persona on my program is pretty much the same as my persona off the screen. Except that I have a family. I don’t order my family around like that the same way," she laughed.

The original "Judge Judy" premiered in 1996 and ran for 25 seasons before ending in 2021. Sheindlin later launched "Judy Justice," which concluded in October. She said she was proud of the work her son, Judge Adam Levy, was doing on "Adam's Law" now that he's taken the reins of the family's TV courtroom career after Sheindlin announced she's "rewiring" her career.

"I think he’s certainly smart, and he certainly works very hard at each case," Sheindlin said. "Actually, he works much harder than I did. I think he’s doing a great job and the ratings are backing him up. And I think he’s got an exciting energy and an honorable person, which is what you need behind the bench."

item.title: Pope Leo arrives at hospital for surgery to remove lung nodule
item.description: Pope Leo XIV arrived at Gemelli Hospital in Rome for lung nodule removal after doctors said the growth was identified at a "very early stage."
item.content:encoded:
Pope Leo XIV arrived at Agostino Gemelli University Hospital in Rome for a procedure to remove a small node on his lung on Tuesday.

The 71-year-old pontiff said Monday that doctors discovered the nodule at a "very early stage" and recommended its removal. The surgery is not expected to last long, and the pope is expected to remain hospitalized for approximately one week, according to Vatican spokesman Matteo Bruni.

"Doctors found a small lump in the lung," Leo said after an Angelus address at St. Peter's Square on Monday. "It was identified at a very early stage and well situated."

POPE LEO ANNOUNCES TUMOR ON LUNG, SURGERY PLANNED IN 'NEXT FEW DAYS'

"The doctors consider it appropriate to intervene and so, following their advice, I decided to have surgery to remove it," he continued. "The surgery is already scheduled for the next few days. I thank you for your spiritual closeness and I rely on your prayer."

The surgery is likely to take place within a few days at the Gemelli Hospital in Rome, which is known as the "Pope's" hospital, Vatican sources told Fox News.

POPE LEO XIV BEGINS HISTORIC 4-DAY VISIT TO FRANCE

The Vatican has not disclosed whether the nodule is cancerous, and no further details about the pope's diagnosis or the planned procedure were immediately available.

The announcement comes as a surprise for the American-born pontiff, who has no previously known health problems and is known for maintaining an active lifestyle.

POPE LEO VISITS SITE OF MIRACLE CURES, MEETS PEOPLE WHOSE UNEXPLAINED HEALINGS STUNNED DOCTORS

Leo regularly plays tennis and swims at the papal summer retreat in Castel Gandolfo, according to The Associated Press.

The pope is also scheduled to embark on a major international trip from Nov. 6–17, with planned stops in Uruguay, Argentina and Peru. It remains unclear whether his surgery and recovery will affect those travel plans.

UKRAINE'S ATTACKS ON RUSSIA ARE PUSHING PUTIN CLOSER TO NEGOTIATING TABLE, TRUMP NATO AMBASSADOR SAYS

In addition to addressing his health, Leo used his Sunday remarks to renew his appeal for peace in war-torn Ukraine, warning that the conflict continues to inflict suffering far beyond the country's borders.

"The war in the martyred Ukraine continues to create suffering, even beyond its borders, especially in the poorest countries, where many people depend on the exports of cereals and grains," the pope said.

Fox News' Courtney Walsh and Stephen Sorace contributed to this report.
